title.orig: Sonnet 18: Shall I compare thee to a summer’s day?
title.en: Sonnet 18: Shall I compare thee to a summer’s day?
title.zh: 十四行诗第十八首：我能否把你比作一个夏日

edition.en: Text of the 1609 quarto as given by Project Gutenberg (eBook 1041)
edition.zh: 据古登堡计划电子书 1041 所录 1609 年四开本文本

basis.en: Published in 1609 (Shakespeare’s Sonnets, Thomas Thorpe); the author died in 1616.
basis.zh: 1609 年出版（托马斯·索普印行的《莎士比亚十四行诗》）；作者卒于 1616 年。

note.en: The most quoted of Shakespeare’s 154 sonnets. It begins as a compliment and ends as a claim about writing itself: the summer will fade, but these fourteen lines will keep a person alive for as long as anyone reads them. Every reader who reaches the couplet is, quietly, the proof.
note.zh: 莎士比亚一百五十四首十四行诗中被引用最多的一首。它以赞美开头，以一个关于写作本身的断言收尾：夏天终会褪色，这十四行字却会让一个人一直活着，只要还有人读。每一个读到最后两行的人，都在悄悄替它作证。

excerpt.orig:
So long as men can breathe, or eyes can see,
So long lives this, and this gives life to thee.
excerpt.en:
So long as men can breathe, or eyes can see,
So long lives this, and this gives life to thee.
excerpt.zh:
只要人还能呼吸，眼睛还能看见，
这诗就活着，并且赋予你生命。
